A Randomised Controlled Phase II Trial of Temozolomide With or Without Cannabinoids in Patients With Recurrent Glioblastoma

candidate_evidence.quote: To establish whether the addition of cannabinoids (Nabiximols) to standard TMZ treatment improves overall survival time (OS) in MGMT methylated recurrent GBM compared to the addition of placebo to TMZ.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: First recurrence of GBM planned for systemic treatment as determined by local Multidisciplinary Team (MDT)

role_evidence.quote: The trial will randomise a target number of 120 patients on a 2:1 basis to receive either Nabiximols or Nabiximols-matched placebo, in combination with standard TMZ.

agents.drug_class_hint: cannabinoid (delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol component of nabiximols/Sativex; licensed for MS spasticity)

coder_notes: Nabiximols (Sativex) split into its fixed-dose components dronabinol (THC) and cannabidiol, each experimental_monotherapy per R3. No antitumour mechanism is stated in the record. Temozolomide given in both arms = soc_backbone. Placebo listed as control_comparator. IDH-wildtype used to define GBM; MGMT methylation is an entry requirement but never candidate-matched. Exclusion of BRAF-mutant/PXA-like tumours serves to confirm IDH-WT GBM diagnosis; not recorded as a separate biomarker. Ages include CHILD (age >=16).
